question.prompt: What web start URL should these ORBITAL navigation tests open? The corpus names no runnable address for the dashboard.

options.label: Use {{start_url}}
options.detail: Keep the shared {{start_url}} placeholder in every web test and replace it at execution time.

options.label: Provide actual URL
options.detail: Supply the concrete ORBITAL dashboard URL to replace the placeholder in all tests.

options.label: Defer URL
options.detail: Leave the tests authored but not runnable until a web start URL is available.

content.risk_rationale: All seven tests are web-surface checks and cannot run until a start URL is supplied; the behavior design is grounded, but execution remains blocked without an entry point.

content.title: Keep single-page state across repeated sidebar switches

check.operand: application routing, separate dashboard pages, navigation to another URL, or a multi-page workflow caused by sidebar navigation

content.test_md_blob:
# Keep single-page state across repeated sidebar switches

> Prove repeated sidebar changes across primary, analytics, research, and system contexts keep the dashboard in the same single-page shell while the active item and workspace heading update in place.

## Step 1

Open ORBITAL at {{start_url}} in a fresh browser session.

## Step 2

Store the current browser URL as baseline_url, the current workspace heading as heading_1, and the active sidebar item as active_1.

## Step 3

In the left sidebar, activate the Portfolio item in the PRIMARY section; store the resulting workspace heading as heading_2 and the resulting active sidebar item as active_2.

## Step 4

Assert the current browser URL still equals baseline_url, active_2 is Portfolio, and heading_2 differs from heading_1.

## Step 5

In the left sidebar, activate the Performance item in the ANALYTICS section; store the resulting workspace heading as heading_3 and the resulting active sidebar item as active_3.

## Step 6

Assert the current browser URL still equals baseline_url, active_3 is Performance, and heading_3 differs from heading_2.

## Step 7

In the left sidebar, activate the Research Notes item in the RESEARCH section; store the resulting workspace heading as heading_4 and the resulting active sidebar item as active_4.

## Step 8

Assert the current browser URL still equals baseline_url, active_4 is Research Notes, and heading_4 differs from heading_3.

## Step 9

In the left sidebar, activate the Alerts item in the SYSTEM section; store the resulting workspace heading as heading_5 and the resulting active sidebar item as active_5.

## Step 10

Assert the current browser URL still equals baseline_url, active_5 is Alerts, and heading_5 differs from heading_4.

## Step 11 — assert @verifies ac-1, ac-7, ac-8

Confirm 'application routing, separate dashboard pages, navigation to another URL, or a multi-page workflow caused by sidebar navigation' does NOT appear (forbidden-presence) — the stated promise: Activating a sidebar navigation item keeps the application within the same page instead of routing away.

content.test_md_blob:
# Use keyboard navigation to switch dashboard context in place

> Prove the sidebar can be operated by keyboard so a focused navigation item becomes active and updates the workspace heading without leaving the current page.

## Step 1

Open ORBITAL at {{start_url}} in a fresh browser session.

## Step 2

Store the current browser URL as baseline_url, the current workspace heading as baseline_heading, and the active sidebar item as baseline_active.

## Step 3

Using keyboard navigation only in the left sidebar, move focus to the Risk item in the ANALYTICS section and confirm the focused item shows a visible focus indicator.

## Step 4

Activate the focused Risk item from the keyboard; store the resulting workspace heading as updated_heading and the resulting active sidebar item as updated_active.

## Step 5

Assert the current browser URL still equals baseline_url, updated_active is Risk and differs from baseline_active, and updated_heading differs from baseline_heading.

## Step 6 — assert @verifies ac-10, ac-1, ac-7, ac-8

Confirm presence check: a visible focus indicator on the currently focused sidebar navigation item (exists) — the stated promise: A focused sidebar navigation item shows visible focus during keyboard navigation.

# Show the default Overview shell on first load

> Prove the dashboard shell starts with the full sidebar inventory visible, Overview selected by default, and the initial workspace heading already aligned to that default context.

## Step 1

Open ORBITAL at {{start_url}} in a fresh browser session.

## Step 2

Inspect the left sidebar and confirm the PRIMARY, ANALYTICS, RESEARCH, and SYSTEM sections show Overview, Portfolio, Markets, Watchlist, Transactions, Performance, Risk, Attribution, Scenarios, Research Notes, Saved Views, Reports, Alerts, and Data Health.

## Step 3

Confirm Overview is the active sidebar item on first load.

## Step 4

Confirm the main workspace heading reads Portfolio Overview.

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-2, ac-3, ac-4, ac-5, ac-6, ac-9

Confirm absolute check: Portfolio Overview (equals) — the stated promise: On first load, the workspace heading is Portfolio Overview.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because repeated cross-section switching is the strongest chance to expose unintended routing, stale heading updates, or active-state drift in the single-page shell.
[value_score] Scored next because keyboard operation and visible focus are explicit accessibility requirements and regressions here make the navigation unreachable for keyboard users.
[value_score] Scored next because the initial load proves the default Overview state, initial heading, and full sidebar inventory that anchor every later navigation path.
[value_score] Scored next because a representative PRIMARY switch proves the most central top-level context change beyond the default state.
[value_score] Scored next because an ANALYTICS switch proves the same in-place navigation contract on a different section family.
[value_score] Scored next because a RESEARCH switch extends representative family coverage for the same shell behavior.
[value_score] Scored last among the kept set because a SYSTEM switch completes section-family coverage with the lowest incremental risk among the representative clicks.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check stayed on the highest-risk no-routing promise while the steps corroborate active-item and heading updates after each switch. Technique fit: the multi-hop sequence matches the edge/state-flow risk. Negative gap: no invalid-navigation case was added because the source defines no disabled or forbidden sidebar action. Assert breadth: kept assertions to URL stability, selected item, and heading change only.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check directly proves the keyboard-path focus requirement while the steps corroborate in-place activation and no routing. Technique fit: the a11y path matches the source's keyboard operation and visible focus requirements. Negative gap: no inaccessible-focus negative case was added because the source gives no alternate failure-mode behavior to test. Assert breadth: kept assertions to focus visibility, target activation, heading change, and URL stability.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check anchors the exact initial heading named by the source while the steps cover sidebar inventory and default active item. Technique fit: initial-load equivalence partitioning is appropriate because this is the single default-state path. Negative gap: no empty or missing-sidebar case was added because the source specifies only the required initial shell, not degraded states. Assert breadth: kept assertions to listed navigation items, default selection, and initial heading.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check uses the active-item state transition promised by the source, and the steps corroborate no routing and heading change. Technique fit: one representative PRIMARY click is appropriate because the source gives the same navigation behavior for the family. Negative gap: no invalid PRIMARY target case was added because the source names no unavailable PRIMARY item state. Assert breadth: kept assertions to active item, heading change, and URL stability.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check uses the active-item state transition promised by the source, and the steps corroborate no routing and heading change. Technique fit: one representative ANALYTICS click is appropriate because the source gives the same navigation behavior for the family. Negative gap: no invalid ANALYTICS target case was added because the source names no unavailable ANALYTICS item state. Assert breadth: kept assertions to active item, heading change, and URL stability.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check uses the active-item state transition promised by the source, and the steps corroborate no routing and heading change. Technique fit: one representative RESEARCH click is appropriate because the source gives the same navigation behavior for the family. Negative gap: no invalid RESEARCH target case was added because the source names no unavailable RESEARCH item state. Assert breadth: kept assertions to active item, heading change, and URL stability.
